5 Year Revenue & EBITDA Estimates

February 24, 2026
Sample report of Indiamart Intermesh

5-Year Revenue & EBITDA Estimates: Growth Sputters to 12% — Can ARPU Expansion Offset Stagnant Supplier Additions?

Executive Snapshot:

  • Thesis: Indiamart is transitioning from a volume-led growth story to an ARPU-led cash compounder. With standalone collection growth decelerating to 8% (Q2 FY26) and paying supplier growth nearly stalling (+2% YoY), the company is relying heavily on pricing power within its Gold/Platinum tiers (Top 10% contribute ~47% of revenue).
  • Key Driver: ARPU Expansion (~65% of future growth). With volume growth capped by high churn in the 'Silver' bucket, future revenue hinges on moving existing 222K suppliers up the value chain.
  • Critical Dependency: Churn Management. Management has admitted that churn in the monthly/annual Silver bucket remains “stubborn.” If this bleeds into Gold/Platinum tiers, the thesis breaks.
  • Watch: Standalone Collection Growth, currently lagging at 8-10%; needs to cross 15% to justify premium valuations.

Competitive Position & Scenario Probabilities

Competitive Position: Wide Moat (Network Effects) — The platform holds a dominant liquidity advantage with 222K paying suppliers and 42M active buyers. However, the moat is Stable rather than widening. While network effects protect against new entrants, they are not currently driving new usage velocity at the bottom of the pyramid (Silver tier churn is high), indicating saturation or value-proposition mismatch for smaller SMEs.

Scenario Probability Key Drivers
Base Case 55-60% Supplier base grows 3-4% CAGR; Revenue growth driven by 8-10% ARPU hikes; Margins stabilize ~35% due to reduced acquisition spend.
Bear Case 25-30% Elevated risk. Triggered if Standalone Collections growth stays <10% for 2 more quarters OR if entry-level churn forces price rollbacks. (See Section 5).
Bull Case 15-20% Requires specific breakout in 'Busy Infotech' scaling (>30% CAGR) AND successful stabilization of Silver bucket churn leading to >6K net adds/quarter.

Probability Rationale

Base case probability is anchored by the persistent disconnect between management's aspiration (20%+ growth) and actual delivery (12% Consolidated Revenue growth in Q2 FY26). The Bear case is elevated above standard 20% because the core standalone engine shows signs of saturation (net additions were negative in Q3 FY25 and only modestly recovered to +2.8K in Q2 FY26).

This section breaks down the total projected revenue increase (Base Case) into its component drivers.

ARPU Expansion & Tier Migration (~60% / Rs.648 Cr)

  • Assumed CAGR: 8%
  • Base (FY25): Annualized Revenue per Supplier Rs.61K.
  • Target (FY30): ~Rs.90K.
  • Rationale: Top 10% of customers contribute ~47% of revenue. Growth relies on migrating Silver users to Gold/Platinum. Pricing power remains intact in the top tier despite churn at the bottom.

Net New Supplier Volume (~20% / Rs.216 Cr)

  • Assumed CAGR: 3%
  • Base (FY25): 217K Paying Suppliers.
  • Target (FY30): ~255K Paying Suppliers.
  • Rationale: Q2 FY26 Net adds were only ~2.8K (normalized). High churn in the 'Silver' monthly bucket severely caps volume growth. Est assumes modest recovery but no return to pre-2022 volume velocity.

Accounting Software (Busy Infotech) (~15% / Rs.162 Cr)

  • Assumed CAGR: 22%
  • Base (FY25): ~Rs.66 Cr Rev (Busy).
  • Target (FY30): ~Rs.228 Cr.
  • Rationale: Busy Q2 FY26 billing grew 57% (normalized). This segment is growing faster than core B2B but on a smaller base.

Other Income/Adjacencies (~5% / Rs.54 Cr)

  • Assumed CAGR: 10%
  • Rationale: Incremental revenue from Vyapar, Livekeeping, and new SaaS initiatives.

Key Assumptions & Risk Assessment

4.1 Revenue Growth Assumptions

  • Supplier Stagnation: Projections assume paying suppliers grow at a pedestrian 3-4% CAGR. Management's pivot to “quality over quantity” (reducing suppliers introduced per buyer from 9-10 to 4-5) explicitly limits volume explosion to preserve buyer experience.
  • Pricing Power: Assumes 6-8% annual ARPU increase. If macro headwinds force a price rollback to retain Silver customers, the Base Case is invalid.
  • Busy Infotech: Assumed to grow at 20%+; however, recent policy changes (channel partner payout restructuring in Nov '24) create short-term noise.

4.2 Margin Trajectory Rationale

  • Cost Control Floor: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin was ~33% (Consolidated) and ~32% (Standalone). Management guided that margins remain elevated due to lower subscriber acquisition costs (deliberately slowing sales spend).
  • Terminal Margin: Capped at 40%. The business has immense operating leverage, but sustaining >40% usually invites aggressive competition or requires massive reinvestment.

4.3 Key Risks to Estimates

  • Churn Persistence: If churn moves from the “Silver” bucket (entry-level) to the “Gold” bucket, the 60% revenue driver (ARPU) collapses.
  • Collections Lag: Standalone collections grew only 8% in Q2 FY26. Revenue lags collections. If collections don't accelerate, FY27 revenue estimates are at risk.

4.4 Execution/Credibility Note

  • Adjustment Applied: Estimates are heavily discounted from implied management aspirations. While management targets “double-digit” customer growth historically, actual net adds (2K-3K/quarter) imply only ~4-5% growth. We have modeled the actual trajectory (3-4%), not the aspiration.

4.5 Data Limitations

  • Churn Granularity: Exact churn rates by specific tier (Silver Monthly vs Annual vs Gold) are not disclosed, forcing analyst estimates based on qualitative commentary.

Scenario Triggers

Bear Case (FY30 Revenue Rs.2,050 Cr, 25-30% Prob):

  • Trigger 1: Standalone Collections growth drops below 5% for two consecutive quarters (indicating pricing power exhaustion).
  • Trigger 2: Net Paying Supplier additions turn negative again (as they did in Q3 FY25), shrinking the base to <210K.

Bull Case (FY30 Revenue Rs.3,360 Cr, 15-20% Prob):

  • Trigger 1: “Busy Infotech” billing growth accelerates >30% sustainably, becoming a material revenue pillar (>10% of consol revenue).
  • Trigger 2: Silver tier churn reduces significantly due to product interventions, returning net supplier additions to >6K/quarter.

Analyst Watchlist

  1. Standalone Customer Collections (Q3/Q4 FY26): Must exceed 12% YoY growth. Current 8% growth (Q2 FY26) is a flashing yellow light for future revenue.
  2. Net Paying Supplier Additions: Watch if this metric stabilizes above 4,000/quarter. The Q3 FY25 dip (-3.5K) and Q2 FY26 recovery (+2.8K normalized) show volatility.
  3. Busy Infotech Billing: Monitor the “normalized” growth post-channel partner payout restructuring. If it sustains >40%, this could re-rate the multiple.
  4. Unique Business Enquiries: Growth here (12% in Q2 FY26) is healthy. If this decouples from supplier growth, it indicates a monetization failure, not a traffic failure.

  • Swaraj Engines makes diesel engines and spare parts for tractors.
  • It sells entirely to its 52% promoter Mahindra & Mahindra, via that promoter's tractor business, the Swaraj Division.

  • It carries no debt. It funds spending from internal accruals.
  • Near-term profit depends mainly on finishing the tractor-engine expansion while holding operating margin near 13.6%.

      FAQs on Swaraj Engines Ltd. Business

      What does Swaraj Engines do?

      Swaraj Engines Ltd. manufactures and supplies diesel engines ranging from 22 HP to over 65 HP, along with high-tech engine components using productive and precise quality analyzing machines.

      Who are the competitors of Swaraj Engines?

      Swaraj Engines major competitors are Greaves Cotton, Sunrise Effnt. Mkt., Kirloskar Oil Engine, Cummins India, Sanghvi Movers, Windsor Machines, Kabra Extrus.technik.
      Market Cap of Swaraj Engines is ₹4,241 Crs.
      While the median market cap of its peers are ₹3,213 Crs.

      Is Swaraj Engines financially stable compared to its competitors?

      Swaraj Engines seems to be financially stable compared to its competitors.
      The probability of it going bankrupt or facing a financial crunch seem to be lower than its immediate competitors.
